Individual times-table practice

The 12 times table.
Recall it. Turn it around. Use it.

Combine ten groups and two groups. Connect to grouping, time and measures where appropriate. The academy keeps checking facts on later days and mixes them with earlier learning.

One fact, several connections

12 × 6 = 726 × 12 = 7272 ÷ 12 = 612 × □ = 72

Say what the groups mean. Draw an array or use counters when a fact needs more support. After the idea is clear, practise recalling the answer independently rather than only counting through the table from the beginning.

Practise the parts that need attention

The table tracker records multiplication, inverse division and missing-factor evidence. Match-fit status requires successful later-day recall, with broad fact coverage. Seeing an answer in a worked example is useful learning, but is recorded differently from an independent answer.

Short sessions allow facts to return after a gap. A table does not become permanently secure from one perfect run, so the adaptive route keeps earlier facts in practice while the learner builds new skills.
